title: The canonical Roos, strict-limit and intrinsic Koszul units agree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ use the small pro-etale site, the completed ring sheaf $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/t^n)_W$, the constant quotient sheaves $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$ and the unbounded derived category $D(R_W)$ of sheaves of $R_W$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All quotient modules are restricted to $R_W$ along the specified limit projections. Let $W$ be any scheme and $K\in D(R_W)$. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, set $U_n=P\otimes_{R_W}S_{W,n}$ and $V_n=P\otimes_{R_W}[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$, with quotient transitions on $U$ and $(t,1)$ on the two-term factors of $V$. Write $\mathsf C(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod Z_n\to\prod Z_n)[-1]$ for the strict Roos model, with coordinates $(y,x)$ and differential $(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Let $\eta_U:K\to\mathsf C(U)$ and $\eta_V:K\to\mathsf C(V)$ be induced by the strict quotient and degree-zero Koszul augmentations with zero shifted-product component. Let $F(P)$ and $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}:K\to F(P)$ be the explicit intrinsic Koszul fiber and its unit [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. The coordinate map $j_P:F(P)\to\mathsf C(V)$, $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$, is a chain isomorphism sending $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}$ to $\eta_V$. If $a:V\to U$ is induced by the quotient augmentations and $\rho$ is the normalized strict Roos comparison, the natural isomorphism
$$d_K=\rho_U\circ\mathsf C(a)\circ j_P:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U$$
satisfies $d_K\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}=\rho_U\eta_U=\operatorname{comp}_K$, where $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is the canonical derived strict quotient-augmentation map. These identifications descend independently of $P$. If $K$ is derived complete in the prescribed Roos-triangle sense [def-weil-derived-complete], then $\eta_U$, $\operatorname{comp}_K$ and the actual intrinsic unit $\eta_K^{\mathrm{intr}}$ are isomorphisms. No boundedness, constructibility or finiteness condition on $W$ is assumed. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $K[r]$ is again Roos-triangle derived complete whenever $K$ is, and the same conclusions apply to its shifted representative $P[r]$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement] with the given $A,t,W,P$. It verifies the adic-datum hypotheses for $(A,(t))$, identifies the specified quotient projection with $R_W/t^nR_W$, and gives the strict tower map $a:V\to U$ as a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. In particular the principal Koszul tower here is the one in the intrinsic definition, with precisely the transitions $(t,1)$. Countable products of $R_W$-module sheaves are exact by [det-pe-products-exact] (products over any index set are exact on the pro-etale site), so the hypotheses of the strict Roos comparison hold on this site. Work in a common universe in which the small pro-etale site and its module sheaves have the sizes required there.

proof.text: Put $B=\prod_n V_n$ and $f=1-s$. The intrinsic definition gives $F(P)^i=B^i\oplus B^{i-1}$ and $d_F(x,y)=(dx,fx-dy)$; the strict model gives $\mathsf C(V)^i=B^{i-1}\oplus B^i$ and $d_{\mathsf C}(y,x)=(-dy-fx,dx)$. Consequently $d_{\mathsf C}j_P(x,y)=(dy-fx,dx)=j_Pd_F(x,y)$. The inverse is $(y,x)\mapsto(x,-y)$. This proves the chain isomorphism, including its sign, directly. Writing $u_V:P\to B$ for the product of the degree-zero Koszul units, the intrinsic unit is $p\mapsto(u_Vp,0)$, so $j_P$ carries it to $(0,u_Vp)$, exactly $\eta_V$. The coordinate formulas also commute with every chain map $P\to P\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; explicit signed cone and strict augmentation refinement written by Q67

proof.text: Let $u_{U,n}:P\to U_n$ be the quotient tensor unit and $u_{V,n}:P\to V_n$ the degree-zero Koszul tensor unit. On the two-term Koszul factor, the composite of the degree-zero inclusion $R_W[0]\to Q_{W,n}$ and $\epsilon_n:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$ is the specified quotient $R_W\to S_{W,n}$. Tensoring this equality gives $a_nu_{V,n}=u_{U,n}$. The source transition fixes the degree-zero unit and the quotient transitions compose with the quotient units, so these families are strictly compatible, and $fu_U=fu_V=0$ in the respective products. The strict Roos map is the product of $a_n$ in both coordinates. Thus $\mathsf C(a)\eta_V=(0,(a_nu_{V,n})_n)=(0,(u_{U,n})_n)=\eta_U$ as chain maps, with no choice of a homotopy. In Lean the cokernel/cone identity computes the actual degree-zero augmentation.

proof.text: Use exact countable products [det-pe-products-exact], the Grothendieck abelian structure of $R_W$-module sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and the strict Roos quasi-isomorphism theorem to invert the Koszul-to-quotient comparison after Q. For any K-injective resolution q of the quotient tower, set rho to Q(Roos(q)) followed by the inverse of Q(roos inclusion). The ordinary-limit augmentation is the limit lift of the compatible family q_n u_U,n. Naturality of the zero-shifted-component Roos augmentation proves its exact normalization with rho, including the equation with the intrinsic unit through the signed fiber isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply the unconditional total-tensor/scalar-reduction tower isomorphism, with its actual unit and naturality identities. Apply the Roos functor to this isomorphism. The elementary generic Roos-map and mapping-cocone lift identities show that the quotient augmentation is sent to IntegralOnSlice.roosUnit. Transport the existing completionComparison along this isomorphism; use completionUnit_existsUnique for the normalized quotient descent. Define FI=FU=completion, unitI=comp=completionUnit, d=identity and transport the representative intrinsic comparison through the inverse of Q(j followed by Roos(a)). Cancel those isomorphisms to prove both naturality and unit equations. No finite scalar extension is involved.

Choose a finite-field datum of characteristic different from ell, using a prime larger than ell and coefficient_datum. The existing localization of flat-term K-flat complexes is essentially surjective, so choose a good representative under qGood. Apply roosIntrinsicCompletenessEquivalence, equivalence (i) with (v), to conclude that the actual completionUnit is invertible for a Roos-complete K. Naturality carries this to any representative of K. The quotient and intrinsic representative normalizations then imply invertibility of their actual units by cancelling the representative isomorphisms.

For shift stability use equivalence (i) with (ii) in roosIntrinsicCompletenessEquivalence: completeness is vanishing of the specified local derived Hom tests. Exact restriction commutes with shift, and the right internal-Hom functor commutes with shift; an isomorphism transports a zero object to a zero object. Hence all tests still vanish for K[r], giving completeness. The existing proved shift_kFlat lemma of KFlatFixedTensorTriangulated gives K-flatness of P[r]; its terms are the reindexed flat terms of P. Shift the representative isomorphism via Q.commShiftIso, and apply the already proved complete-unit clauses to this good shifted representative.
